mainTopic: Lashes for improperly cooked קרבן פסח and לאו שבכללות; the timing of the לאוין of נא, מבושל, and eating the פסח by day
overview: The amud opens by counting the מלקות for eating the קרבן פסח undercooked (נא) or boiled (מבושל). Each counts as two sets, and both together count as three, because 'כי אם צלי אש' is treated as an extra לאו. אביי disagrees: there are no מלקות for a לאו שבכללות. One version of his view gives one set of lashes for it, and another version gives none, since only a specific לאו like חסימה brings מלקות. The same dispute is repeated for a נזיר who eats grape skins and pits. Next, ברייתות teach that the לאו of נא applies only at night, when the מצוה of eating צלי applies. This is learned from the extra words 'כי אם צלי אש'. רבי learns from the doubled phrase 'בשל מבשל' that meat boiled by day is also forbidden when eaten at night. Finally, a ברייתא makes eating roasted פסח meat by day a לאו like נא. The גמרא finds a source in 'בלילה הזה' but objects that a לאו הבא מכלל עשה is only an עשה. רב חסדא begins his answer by asking whose view the ברייתא follows, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Counting the lashes for eating the פסח undercooked or boiled
steps.stepSummary: The ruling continues: undercooked gets two sets of lashes, boiled gets two, and undercooked plus boiled gets three.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One who ate it undercooked] receives two sets of lashes. Boiled: he receives two sets of lashes. Undercooked and boiled: he receives three sets of lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ruling that began earlier. It counts how many sets of מלקות a person gets for eating the קרבן פסח without roasting it properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has a specific לאו against נא and another against מבושל. It also says 'כי אם צלי אש', which this view counts as one more separate לאו. So each specific violation adds one set to the general one: נא gives 1+1=2, מבושל gives 1+1=2, and both together give 1+1+1=3.

keyTerms.meaning: receives lashes (מלקות)
undercooked, only partially roasted
boiled or cooked in liquid
roasted directly by fire, the required way to eat the פסח

steps.confusionAlert: The number of lashes is not simply 'one per bad cooking method.' The count is always one higher, because the general command 'כי אם צלי אש' is counted as an extra לאו on top of the specific ones.

phrases.english: [If he ate it undercooked] he receives two sets of lashes.
phrases.notes: Still the earlier case: one set for the לאו against eating it נא, and one for 'כי אם צלי אש'.

phrases.english: Boiled: he receives two sets of lashes.
phrases.notes: One set for the לאו of בשל מבושל, one for 'כי אם צלי אש'.

phrases.english: Undercooked and boiled: he receives three sets of lashes.
phrases.notes: One set each for נא, for מבושל, and for 'כי אם צלי אש'.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹקֶה שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ruling begun earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נא gives two sets of lashes, מבושל gives two, and נא plus מבושל gives three, because 'כי אם צלי אש' counts as an additional לאו.

steps.title: אביי: no lashes for a general prohibition
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that a לאו שבכללות, a prohibition covering many things at once, does not bring מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: One does not receive lashes for a prohibition that is stated in general terms.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי disagrees with the count we just saw. He says the general command 'כי אם צלי אש' cannot add lashes, because it is a broad prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כי אם צלי אש' forbids every way of preparing the meat other than roasting, so it covers many cases at once. אביי holds that such a broad לאו does not carry מלקות. That knocks out the 'extra' set of lashes in the earlier count.

keyTerms.meaning: one does not receive lashes
a general prohibition that includes several different things in one לאו
אביי, a major אמורא of Babylonia

steps.whatToRemember: A לאו שבכללות is one prohibition that covers many different things. אביי says no מלקות are given for it.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle 'אין לוקין על לאו שבכללות' appears throughout ש"ס and decides when a general prohibition can bring punishment.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
One does not receive lashes for a prohibition stated in general terms.
phrases.notes: This is about 'כי אם צלי אש', which covers נא, מבושל, and other ways of cooking all at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֵין לוֹקִין עַל לָאו שֶׁבִּכְלָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the count of lashes in step 1 by denying lashes for the general לאו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are no מלקות for a לאו שבכללות.

steps.title: First version of אביי: no double lashes, but one set
steps.stepSummary: Some explain that אביי only denies the extra lashes from the general לאו, but one set is still given.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: It is two sets of lashes that he does not receive, but one set at any rate he does receive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first of two versions of what אביי meant. In this version, his rule is narrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the general לאו cannot pile extra lashes on top of the specific לאו. So the person does not get two sets for one act. But the general לאו is not empty: it can still produce one set of lashes. For example, if someone violated it in a way not covered by a specific לאו, he would be lashed for 'כי אם צלי אש' alone.

keyTerms.meaning: some say; introduces another version of a statement
two
at least one, at any rate one

phrases.english: Some say:
it is two sets of lashes that he does not receive,
phrases.notes: He doesn't get an extra set for the general לאו.

phrases.english: but at any rate one set he does receive.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: תַּרְתֵּי הוּא דְּלָא לָקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the scope of אביי's principle in a narrow way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לאו שבכללות does not add a second set of lashes, but it can still bring one set.

steps.title: Second version of אביי: no lashes at all, unlike muzzling
steps.stepSummary: Others explain that a general לאו brings no lashes at all, because it is not specific like the לאו of חסימה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: He does not receive even one set of lashes, because his prohibition is not specific, like the prohibition of muzzling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second version of אביי, which is broader. Here a general לאו brings no lashes at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of מלקות are learned from the לאו of 'לא תחסום שור בדישו', which sits right next to the פסוקים about lashes. Only a לאו that resembles חסימה, a single prohibition about one specific thing, brings lashes. A general לאו like 'כי אם צלי אש' does not fit that model, so it brings zero lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: even one
its prohibition is specific, focused on one thing
the לאו against muzzling an ox while it threshes, the model for which לאוין bring lashes

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of אביי. In the first, a לאו שבכללות brings one set of lashes but never an extra one. In the second, it brings no lashes at all, because only a specific לאו like חסימה brings מלקות.
steps.whyThisMatters: The comparison to the לאו of חסימה is the standard source that sets the conditions for מלקות.

phrases.english: Some say:
he does not receive even one set of lashes,
because his prohibition is not specific
phrases.notes: It covers many different methods of preparation at once.

phrases.english: like the prohibition of muzzling.
phrases.notes: 'לא תחסום שור בדישו' (דברים כה:ד), placed next to the פסוקים about lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: חֲדָא נָמֵי לָא לָקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a broader, competing version of אביי's principle than step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לאו שבכללות brings no lashes at all, since only a specific לאו like חסימה brings מלקות.

steps.title: רבא: a נזיר who eats grape skins or pits gets extra lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a נזיר who eats a זג gets two sets of lashes, a חרצן gets two, and both together get three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If a נזיר ate a grape skin, he gets two sets of lashes. A grape pit, two sets. A grape skin and a grape pit, three sets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case with the same structure as the פסח case: a נזיר eating grape skins and pits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids the נזיר to eat skins and pits with specific words. It also has one broad לאו against anything from the grapevine ("מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין"). רבא counts the specific לאו plus the broad one. So a skin gets two sets of lashes, a pit gets two, and both together get three, since the broad לאו is counted only once.

keyTerms.meaning: Grape skin
Grape pit / seed
A person who took a vow to avoid grape products, haircuts, and contact with the dead
He receives lashes

phrases.english: Rava said: If [a nazir] ate a grape skin
phrases.notes: The case is a נזיר, as in במדבר ו:ד.

phrases.english: he receives two sets of lashes.
phrases.notes: One for the skin, one for the general 'grapevine product' לאו.

phrases.english: A grape pit: he receives two sets of lashes.
A skin and a pit: he receives three sets of lashes.
phrases.notes: One set each for the skin, the pit, and the general לאו.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אָכַל זָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels רבא's פסח ruling (Step 1) in the case of a נזיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The general לאו of a נזיר adds a set of lashes on top of the specific לאו for skins or pits.

steps.title: אביי: no lashes for the נזיר's general prohibition
steps.stepSummary: אביי repeats his rule that a לאו שבכללות does not bring lashes, now about the נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: One does not receive lashes for a prohibition stated in general terms.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי disagrees with רבא about the נזיר using the same rule he used for פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the broad לאו "מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין" covers many items at once, so it is a לאו שבכללות. It cannot add lashes, so רבא's extra set falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: One does not receive lashes

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a copy error. The גמרא really repeats אביי's words, because the same argument applies in a new case: the נזיר instead of the פסח.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
One does not receive lashes for a general prohibition.
phrases.notes: Here this refers to 'anything made from the grapevine'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֵין לוֹקִין עַל לָאו שֶׁבִּכְלָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבא's ruling in Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נזיר's general grapevine לאו does not bring lashes.

steps.title: First version: only the extra lashes are cancelled
steps.stepSummary: Some explain that אביי only cancels the double lashes. The נזיר still gets one set.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: It is two sets that he does not get, but at least one set he does get.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first explanation of how far אביי's rule goes in the נזיר case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the general לאו cannot stack on top of the specific one. The person is still punished once. So eating a skin brings one set of lashes, not two.

keyTerms.meaning: Two
At any rate / at least

phrases.english: Some say:
it is two sets that he does not receive,
but at any rate one set he does receive.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: תַּרְתֵּי הוּא דְּלָא לָקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the scope of אביי's rule from Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the added set of lashes is cancelled. One set remains.

steps.title: Second version: the general prohibition brings no lashes at all
steps.stepSummary: Others explain that a general לאו brings no lashes at all, because it is not specific like the לאו of חסימה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: He does not get even one set, because his prohibition is not specific like the prohibition of muzzling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second, stricter explanation of אביי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes are learned from the לאו of חסימה, which forbids one specific act. A broad לאו that covers many things is not like it, so it cannot bring lashes even once.

keyTerms.meaning: Specific / singled out
Also / even

steps.whatToRemember: With both פסח and נזיר, רבא counts the general לאו as an extra set of lashes. אביי says a לאו שבכללות does not add lashes. One version of אביי gives one set; the other gives none for the general לאו.

phrases.english: And some say:
he does not receive even one set,
because his prohibition is not specific
like the prohibition of muzzling.
phrases.notes: That's the לאו we learn the rules of lashes from.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: חֲדָא נָמֵי לָא לָקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative reading to Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A general לאו brings no lashes at all, since it is not specific like חסימה.

steps.title: Eating partially roasted meat: exempt by day, liable at night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that eating a כזית of נא before nightfall is exempt, but after dark it is punishable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If one ate an olive-size of partially roasted meat while it was still day, he is exempt. An olive-size of partially roasted meat after dark, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: when the prohibition of eating the פסח as נא starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לאו of eating נא applies only at night, when the מצוה to eat the פסח applies. Before dark the prohibition is not yet in force, so there is no punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
An olive-size, the minimum amount for liability
While it is still day
After dark

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל כְּזַיִת נָא מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם — פָּטוּר;
phrases.english: If one ate an olive-size of partially roasted meat while still day, he is exempt;
phrases.notes: On the 14th of ניסן, after the פסח was slaughtered.

phrases.english: an olive-size partially roasted after dark, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אָכַל כְּזַיִת נָא מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from counting lashes to the timing of the נא prohibition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נא prohibition applies only after dark.

steps.title: Eating roasted meat by day does not bind one to a group
steps.stepSummary: Eating a כזית of צלי by day does not disqualify a person from his חבורה, but eating it after dark does.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate an olive-size of roasted meat while still day, he has not disqualified himself from the members of his group. An olive-size of roasted meat after dark, he has disqualified himself from the members of the group.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא continues with a parallel rule about roasted meat and group membership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a person really eats the פסח, he is tied to that group and cannot switch. Eating by day does not count as the real eating, because the מצוה only begins at night. So he is still free to eat with his own group.

keyTerms.meaning: Fully roasted, the required way to prepare the פסח
The registered group sharing one קרבן פסח
He disqualified himself

phrases.english: If he ate an olive-size of roasted meat while still day,
he has not disqualified himself from the members of the group;
an olive-size of roasted meat after dark,
he has disqualified himself from the members of the group.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל כְּזַיִת צָלִי מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same ברייתא, parallel to Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating the פסח by day has no legal effect on group membership. Eating it at night does.

steps.title: Another ברייתא proposes that eating partially roasted meat by day should be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא suggests through a קל וחומר that eating נא by day should also be punishable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: One might think that if he ate an olive-size of partially roasted meat while still day, he should be liable. And it is logical: If at the time when he is commanded to eat it roasted, he is forbidden to eat it partially roasted, then at a time when he is not commanded to eat it roasted, is it not logical that he should be forbidden to eat it partially roasted?
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא sets up a possible argument ("יכול") that eating נא by day should be forbidden. This is only a suggestion; the ברייתא will reject it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר goes like this. At night there is a מצוה to eat the meat, and still eating it נא is forbidden. By day there is no מצוה to eat it at all, so it seems eating it נא should be forbidden even more. This seems to contradict Step 9, which says eating נא by day is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Another ברייתא taught
One might think (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
And it is logical (introduces a קל וחומר)
A positive command: arise and eat
A negative command: do not eat

steps.confusionAlert: The word "יכול" means this is NOT the final halacha. It is an argument the ברייתא raises in order to knock it down with a verse.

phrases.english: It was taught in another baraita:
One might think that if he ate an olive-size of partially roasted meat
while still day, he should be liable,
and it is logical:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּקוּם אֱכוֹל צָלִי —
phrases.english: If at the time when he is under the command 'arise, eat it roasted',
he is under 'do not eat it partially roasted';
then at a time when he is not under 'arise, eat it roasted',

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בְּבַל תֹּאכַל נָא?
phrases.english: is it not logical that he is under 'do not eat it partially roasted'?

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: יָכוֹל אָכַל כְּזַיִת נָא מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם יְהֵא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a logical argument that seems to contradict Step 9's exemption by day; it sets up the verse-based answer that comes next.
steps.raayaObject: The suggestion that eating נא by day is punishable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר: if the לאו applies when there is a מצוה of eating, it should surely apply when there is none.

steps.title: The opposite logic: maybe נא is forbidden only when צלי is not commanded
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes back on the קל וחומר and offers the reverse rule: when there is no מצוה to eat צלי (by day), נא is forbidden, and when there is a מצוה to eat צלי (at night), נא is not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is not so: at a time when one is not under the command 'arise and eat roasted,' he is under the prohibition 'do not eat partially roasted.' At a time when one is under the command 'arise and eat roasted,' he is not under the prohibition 'do not eat partially roasted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the קל וחומר from step 11 by showing that the opposite logic is just as reasonable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 argued that if נא is forbidden at night, when eating is allowed, it should surely be forbidden by day. Here the ברייתא flips it: maybe the prohibition of נא applies only by day, before the meat may be eaten at all. Once night comes and the מצוה of צלי begins, maybe נא is no longer forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps not; this opens the opposite line of reasoning
'Arise and eat roasted': the positive מצוה to eat the פסח roasted at night
'Do not eat partially roasted': the לאו against eating the פסח half-cooked
He is included in, or is not included in, a law

steps.confusionAlert: This reversal is not the final halacha. It is only a 'maybe' that shows the קל וחומר is not airtight. The פסוק in the next steps decides the question.

phrases.english: Or perhaps not:
at a time when he is not under 'arise and eat roasted'
he is under 'do not eat partially roasted';
phrases.notes: By day, before the מצוה starts.

phrases.english: at a time when he is under 'arise and eat roasted'
he is not under 'do not eat partially roasted.'
phrases.notes: At night, once the מצוה applies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ לֹא: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּקוּם אֱכוֹל צָלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 11 by offering equally plausible opposite logic.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר that נא by day should be punishable.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reverse reasoning is just as logical, so the קל וחומר cannot be relied on.

steps.title: Support for the reversal: the meat already became permitted when roasted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the reversal should not seem strange. At night the general ban on eating the פסח is lifted for roasted meat, so maybe the ban on נא is lifted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do not be surprised, for it was released from its general rule regarding roasted meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא backs up the reverse logic of step 12 so it does not sound far-fetched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By day, eating the פסח is forbidden in every form. At night the meat becomes permitted when it is roasted. Since the prohibition was already relaxed at night, one could think the night relaxation also covers נא.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not be surprised
It was released from its general prohibition

phrases.english: And do not be surprised,
for it was released from its general rule regarding roasted.
phrases.notes: At night, roasted meat becomes permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַל תִּתְמַהּ, שֶׁהֲרֵי הוּתַּר מִכְּלָלוֹ אֵצֶל צָלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the reverse logic of step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The reverse logic, that נא may not be forbidden at night.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that at night the general ban on eating the פסח is lifted for צלי.

steps.title: The פסוק decides: נא is forbidden only when the מצוה of צלי applies
steps.stepSummary: The extra words 'כי אם צלי אש' link the לאו of נא to the מצוה of צלי. When one must eat צלי (at night), נא is forbidden. When one need not eat צלי (by day), the לאו of נא does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'Do not eat of it partially roasted, nor boiled in water, but roasted with fire.' There was no need for the verse to say 'but roasted with fire.' So why does it say 'but roasted with fire'? To tell you: at a time when one is under 'arise and eat roasted,' he is under 'do not eat partially roasted.' At a time when one is not under 'arise and eat roasted,' he is not under 'do not eat partially roasted.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since logic could go either way, the ברייתא settles it from an extra phrase in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier פסוק already said to eat the meat 'צלי אש', so repeating it here must teach something new. The extra words tie the לאו of נא to the time of the מצוה of צלי. This rejects both the קל וחומר of step 11 and the reversal of step 12, and confirms the first ברייתא: נא by day is exempt, and נא after dark is punishable.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; introduces a proof from a פסוק
'But roasted with fire': the seemingly extra words in the פסוק
There was no need for the verse to say this, so it comes to teach something
To tell you; introduces the lesson learned

steps.whatToRemember: The לאו of נא is tied to the מצוה of צלי. Both apply only at night. Eating נא by day carries no punishment.
steps.confusionAlert: The wording here mirrors step 12 but is reversed. Step 12 said נא is forbidden when צלי is not commanded. The פסוק teaches the opposite: נא is forbidden only when צלי is commanded.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the first ברייתא (step 9): eating a כזית of נא before nightfall is exempt, and after dark it is punishable.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
'Do not eat of it partially roasted
nor boiled in any way in water,
but roasted with fire,'
phrases.notes: שמות יב:ט

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״כִּי אִם צְלִי אֵשׁ״,
phrases.english: since there is no need for the verse to say 'but roasted with fire,'
phrases.notes: It was already said in the previous פסוק (יב:ח).

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״כִּי אִם צְלִי אֵשׁ״?
phrases.english: so why does the verse say 'but roasted with fire'?
To tell you:
at a time when he is under 'arise and eat roasted'
he is under 'do not eat partially roasted';
at a time when he is not under 'arise and eat roasted'
he is not under 'do not eat partially roasted.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אַל תֹּאכְלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ נָא וּבָשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל בַּמָּיִם כִּי אִם צְלִי אֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the logical back-and-forth of steps 11 to 13 with a proof from the פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The לאו of נא applies only at night, when the מצוה of צלי applies. Eating נא by day is exempt.

steps.title: רבי: the double word בשל מבשל includes meat boiled by day
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns from the extra word 'מבשל' that the prohibition covers meat boiled by day as well as meat boiled after dark, when it is eaten at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: I could have read just 'boiled.' Why does the verse say 'boiled' again? Because I might have thought the rule applies only when it was boiled after dark. From where do we know it applies when it was boiled while still day? The verse says 'boiled, boiled,' meaning in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי adds a new teaching from the doubled word 'בשל מבשל' in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the prohibition applies only at night, one might think only meat boiled at night is forbidden. The extra word 'מבשל' teaches that meat boiled by day is also forbidden if eaten at night. What matters is when it is eaten, not when it was cooked.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא
'Boiled, boiled': a doubled word that includes more cases
After it became dark
While it was still day
In any case

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not saying that eating by day is punishable. He is talking about meat that was boiled by day and then eaten at night.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
I could read just 'boiled';
why does the verse say 'boiled' again?
For I might think I have only
a case where he boiled it after dark;
if he boiled it while still day, from where do we know?
The verse says 'boiled, boiled,' meaning in any case.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֶקְרָא אֲנִי בָּשֵׁל, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר מְבֻשָּׁל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the night-only rule of step 14 and clarifies that the time of cooking does not matter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat of the פסח boiled by day is forbidden when eaten at night, just like meat boiled after dark.

steps.title: רבי already used this phrase for something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי's teaching. He already used ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ to forbid צלי קדר and cooking in other liquids, so how can he use it again for the time of cooking?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי already used this phrase ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ to teach the ban on pot-roasting and the ban on cooking in other liquids!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to רבי's teaching from Step 15. רבי already used the same words for two other laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually one extra word teaches only one law. Earlier, רבי used ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ to teach that the פסח may not be pot-roasted in its own juices (צלי קדר) and may not be cooked in any liquid, not only water. If the phrase is already used up, it seems it cannot also teach about meat cooked by day.

keyTerms.meaning: "Cooked, boiled." A double phrase in the פסוק (שמות יב:ט) about not cooking the פסח
He took it out, meaning he already used this verse for a different teaching
Pot-roasting. Meat cooked in a pot in its own juices, without added liquid
Other liquids besides water, like wine or oil

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the earlier laws are wrong. The question is only whether one phrase can carry an extra teaching on top of what it already teaches.

phrases.english: But this phrase "bashel mevushal"
phrases.notes: The words רבי just used in Step 15

phrases.english: Rabbi already took it out (used it)
for pot-roasting and for other liquids!
phrases.notes: Two laws already learned from this phrase

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ אַפְּקֵיהּ רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source רבי used in Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's derivation from ״מְבֻשָּׁל״ about meat cooked by day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A phrase already used for צלי קדר and other liquids cannot be used again for a new law

steps.title: The unusual wording teaches two laws
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק could have said ״בָּשֵׁל בָּשֵׁל״ or ״מְבֻשָּׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״. Because it switched forms, we learn two separate things from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the phrase only taught about how the meat is cooked, the פסוק should have said either ״בָּשֵׁל בָּשֵׁל״ or ״מְבֻשָּׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״. Why does it say ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The change in the form of the word shows that the פסוק means to teach two different laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating the same word would have been enough for the laws about how the meat is cooked. The פסוק used two different forms, so there is extra meaning. One teaching is about the way of cooking (צלי קדר, other liquids). The other is about the time of cooking (meat cooked by day is also forbidden at night).

keyTerms.meaning: If so. Introduces the argument that the wording would be different if it taught only one thing
Let the פסוק say. Suggests a simpler wording the Torah could have used
Learn two things from it

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how one phrase can be the source for more than one law. The extra teaching comes from the change in the form of the word.

phrases.english: If so
let the verse say either "bashel bashel"
or "mevushal mevushal."
What is meant by "bashel mevushal"?
phrases.notes: He's asking why the פסוק words it this way.

phrases.english: Learn two things from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן לֵימָא קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: the change in word form gives room for an extra teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase is used up by the laws about how the meat is cooked
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase teaches both how the meat is cooked and when it is cooked
steps.whatToRemember: ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ teaches two things: the way the פסח may not be cooked, and that meat cooked even by day may not be eaten at night.

steps.title: A ברייתא: eating roasted meat by day and נא at night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that one who eats roasted פסח meat while it is still day is חייב, and one who eats a כזית of נא after dark is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone ate roasted meat while it was still day, he is liable. And if someone ate an olive-sized piece of partly roasted meat after dark, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with two rulings about eating the פסח. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will learn something from how the ruling is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case is eating meat that is properly roasted but at the wrong time, by day. The second is eating at the right time, at night, but meat that is not properly roasted (נא). Both are called חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: While it is still day, before nightfall
After it got dark
An olive-sized amount, the minimum to be liable for eating
Liable, here meaning liable to lashes

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If one ate roasted meat while it was still day, he is liable,
and an olive-bulk of partly roasted meat after dark, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אָכַל צָלִי מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new ברייתא about the times of eating צלי and נא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating roasted פסח meat by day is חייב, and eating a כזית of נא at night is חייב

steps.title: Roasted meat by day is a לאו, just like נא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists roasted meat together with נא. So just as eating נא is a לאו, eating roasted meat by day is also a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא teaches roasted meat in the same way as partly roasted meat. Just as partly roasted meat is forbidden by a לאו, so too roasted meat eaten by day is forbidden by a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the way the ברייתא lists the two cases side by side. This also prepares the next question: which לאו forbids eating by day?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא did not explain what kind of חיוב applies to eating roasted meat by day. Since it is placed next to נא, which is a clear לאו, the גמרא concludes it is also a full לאו with lashes. Unlike נא, no explicit לאו against eating the פסח by day is obvious, so the גמרא will next ask for its source.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, in the same way as
Forbidden by a negative commandment
Just as ... so too. A formula for comparing two cases

steps.confusionAlert: The ruling about roasted meat by day is not about the meat being badly cooked. The meat is roasted properly. The problem is only the time it is eaten.

phrases.english: It teaches roasted meat similar to partly roasted meat:
just as partly roasted meat is with a prohibition,
so too roasted meat is with a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי צָלִי דּוּמְיָא דְּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the ברייתא in Step 18
steps.raayaObject: That eating roasted פסח meat by day is a full לאו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא lists roasted meat by day right next to נא at night
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows eating the פסח by day is punished with lashes, not just a lighter ban. The גמרא will now look for which פסוק teaches this לאו.

steps.title: Where is the source for the prohibition on roasted meat by day?
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition on נא is written in a פסוק. The גמרא asks what the source is for a prohibition on eating roasted פסח meat during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, for half-roasted meat it is written: 'Do not eat from it half-roasted.' But for roasted meat, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that נא has a clear פסוק. It now asks for the source of the prohibition on eating roasted meat by day, which the ברייתא also called חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 showed that the ברייתא treats roasted meat by day like נא, which is a לאו. But a לאו needs a source in the Torah. For נא there is an explicit 'אל תאכלו'. For roasted meat by day, no such verse is obvious, so the גמרא asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this part is fine
Half-roasted, undercooked meat
Roasted meat
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: Granted, for half-roasted meat, it is written:
'Do not eat from it half-roasted' (Shemos 12:9).
But for roasted meat, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא נָא, כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 19 established that roasted meat by day is a לאו like נא. This step asks for the Torah source of that לאו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for a prohibition on eating roasted פסח meat during the day.

steps.title: The source is 'they shall eat the meat on this night'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says to eat the meat 'on this night.' The גמרא infers that it may be eaten at night but not by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And they shall eat the meat on this night.' At night, yes; by day, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Because the Torah says to eat the meat at night, it is forbidden to eat it during the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself is a positive instruction to eat at night. The גמרא reads it by inference: if the Torah says night, then day is excluded. This gives a prohibition on eating by day, but the prohibition comes only from inference and is not stated directly.

keyTerms.meaning: On this night (the night of פסח)
Yes
No

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And they shall eat the meat on this night' (Shemos 12:8).
At night, yes; by day, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְאָכְלוּ אֶת הַבָּשָׂר בַּלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20 by giving a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'eat the meat on this night' implies that eating it by day is forbidden.

steps.title: A prohibition inferred from a positive command is only an עשה
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition learned from 'at night' is a לאו הבא מכלל עשה. Such a prohibition counts as an עשה, so why does the ברייתא treat it like a real לאו?
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is a prohibition that comes from a positive command, and every prohibition that comes from a positive command counts as a positive command!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. A prohibition learned only by inference from a positive command does not have the strength of a real לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that a לאו הבא מכלל עשה has the status of an עשה. One who breaks it does not get the punishment of a לאו, such as מלקות. So the פסוק from Step 21 cannot explain why the ברייתא lists roasted meat by day together with נא as a real לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition inferred from a positive command
A positive commandment
A negative commandment, which can carry מלקות

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the result is a 'do not' (do not eat by day), its legal status is an עשה, because the Torah only wrote it as a 'do' (eat at night).

phrases.aramaic: הַאי לָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה הוּא,
phrases.english: This is a prohibition that comes by inference from a positive command,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל לָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה — עֲשֵׂה!
phrases.english: and every prohibition that comes from a positive command counts as a positive command!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי לָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in Step 21 as too weak to produce the לאו required by Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation from 'בַּלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה' as the source of a לאו for eating roasted meat by day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inferred prohibition has only the status of an עשה. So it cannot make roasted meat by day a לאו equal to נא, as the ברייתא implies.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks whose opinion the ברייתא follows
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא begins to resolve the problem by asking which תנא the ברייתא follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב חסדא opens his answer by asking which תנא wrote the ברייתא, and the actual answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of finding a new פסוק, רב חסדא will show that the ברייתא follows a specific תנא. That תנא must hold a view that makes roasted meat by day a real לאו. The question 'הא מני' signals that the answer depends on identifying the author.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer
Whose opinion is this?

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: Whose opinion is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הָא מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the קשיא of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution of the ברייתא to a specific תנא (completed on the next amud).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to follow the general rule that a לאו הבא מכלל עשה is only an עשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows a particular תנא whose view yields a real לאו. The details are on the next amud.
